title: Topological spectrum of a directed colimit of rings
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed partially ordered set small in the universe of the rings, let $(A_i,r_{ij}:A_i\to A_j)_{i\le j}$ be a directed system of commutative rings, and let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ with coprojections $r_i:A_i\to A$ be its colimit in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $p_{ij}:\operatorname{Spec}A_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $p_i:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for the induced maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The map $\mathfrak p\mapsto(r_i^{-1}\mathfrak p)_i$ is a homeomorphism from $|\operatorname{Spec}A|$ to the set of families of primes $(\mathfrak p_i)_i$ with $r_{ij}^{-1}(\mathfrak p_j)=\mathfrak p_i$ for every $i\le j$, equipped with the coarsest topology making all coordinate projections continuous. Thus $|\operatorname{Spec}A|$ is the inverse limit of the spaces $|\operatorname{Spec}A_i|$. Moreover, for every $i$ and every quasi-compact open $Q\subseteq|\operatorname{Spec}A_i|$, the open subset $p_i^{-1}(Q)$ is quasi-compact.

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the contractions $\mathfrak p_i=r_i^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$ are prime and compatible, because the maps $r_i$ and $r_{ij}$ compose. Conversely, given compatible primes $\mathfrak p_i$, define $\mathfrak p\subset A$ to consist of those elements represented by some $x_i\in\mathfrak p_i$. The elementwise description of filtered ring colimits gives representatives and says when two representatives agree. Using a common upper bound, compatibility shows that this set is closed under addition and multiplication by arbitrary elements and contains zero but not one. If $r_i(x_i)r_j(y_j)$ lies in it, move $x_i,y_j$ and the witnessing element to one common later stage; primality there puts one factor in the corresponding prime, so one of the original factors lies in $\mathfrak p$. Thus $\mathfrak p$ is prime, and the same common-stage argument gives $r_i^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p_i$. These two constructions are inverse.

For every $i$ and $f\in A_i$, the inverse image of the principal open $D(f)\subset\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ under $p_i$ is $D(r_i(f))\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$: membership is exactly the condition that the relevant element is absent from the prime. Every principal open of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has the form $D(r_i(f))$ for some $i,f$, since every element of $A$ is represented at a stage. Principal opens form a basis for the Zariski topology by the definition of affine spectrum. Hence the topology on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is exactly the coarsest topology making all $p_i$ continuous, and the bijection of Step 1 is a homeomorphism onto the compatible-family inverse-limit topology.

The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is affine, hence quasi-compact by Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact.isCompact_preimage. Apply this directly to the open quasi-compact subset Q. This is the same finite-principal-open argument from Algebra Tag 00E8, already packaged in the Mathlib theorem.

statement_change.what: The original two independent universes allow an index poset larger than the universe of the rings. Smallness must be relative to the ring universe, as in the source set-indexed colimit. Without it the statement is false: take finite subsets of a set larger than the ring universe, with the corresponding finitely generated rational-function fields. A cocone in small rings must be the zero ring, since a nonzero cocone would embed the rational-function field on the whole large set into a small ring. Thus zero is a colimit in the restricted small-ring category, but the zero prime ideals give a compatible family at every field stage. The asserted homeomorphism would identify an empty spectrum with a nonempty space.

Thus $\mathfrak p$ is prime, and the same common-stage argument gives $r_i^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p_i$. These two constructions are inverse.

For every $i$ and $f\in A_i$, the inverse image of the principal open $D(f)\subset\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ under $p_i$ is $D(r_i(f))\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$: membership is exactly the condition that the relevant element is absent from the prime. Hence the topology on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is exactly the coarsest topology making all $p_i$ continuous, and the bijection of Step 1 is a homeomorphism onto the compatible-family inverse-limit topology.

Let $Q\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ be quasi-compact and open. For each point of $Q$, choose a principal open contained in $Q$; quasi-compactness gives finitely many $D(f_1),\ldots,D(f_n)$ covering $Q$. By Step 2, $p_i^{-1}(Q)=\bigcup_{a=1}^nD(r_i(f_a))$. Each principal open $D(r_i(f_a))$ is homeomorphic to the spectrum of the localization $A_{r_i(f_a)}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], hence is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](iii); a finite union of quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact. This proves the final assertion.
